title: Papa Tora’ah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Mentioned in Gittin 19a, where Rav Papa gave him a ruling. Hyman quotes Rashi’s explanation of the epithet as “an ox broker.”

notes.text: The frozen Rashi gloss is סופר של שוורים, “a scribe of oxen.” The consulted Rashi on Gittin19a instead has ספסר של שוורים, “an ox broker.” The textual discrepancy remains open pending the matching scan; the Talmud explicitly names Rav Papa as the one who gave the ruling.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 1029) reads סרסר, “broker,” where the supplied Hebrew reads סופר, “scribe.” The consulted Rashi at Gittin 19a reads ספסר, also “broker,” while the Davidson translation of the Talmud calls Pappa an ox herder. The Talmud distinguishes Rav Pappa, who gave the ruling, from Papa Tora’ah, who received it.
